options.about.title: About
options.about.summary: A local-first password manager: it finds the login fields on a page and fills your username and password, and clicks the sign-in button too when 'Auto-submit login' is on. Entries are encrypted with your master password and stay in this browser on this device.
options.about.featureTotp: Built-in TOTP: the verification code lives with the password, so two-step sign-in gets filled without switching apps
options.about.featureDomain: Exact-host matching keeps dev / test / prod accounts apart, and cross-subdomain matching widens on demand in three tiers
options.about.featureHealth: Offline security check: reuse, weak, common-password and stale entries scored on this machine
options.about.featureTransfer: JSON / CSV import and export, recognising exports from Chrome, LastPass, Bitwarden and 1Password
options.about.featurePanel: Side panel and in-page picker: current-site or full-library search, tag filter, favorites-only, keyboard shortcut
options.about.factStorageValue: Your browser's own storage (chrome.storage.local) — nothing is written to any server
options.about.factCryptoValue: The master password derives the key with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 rounds); username, password, URL, remark and TOTP secret are each encrypted field by field with AES-256-GCM
options.about.factNetworkValue: Two read-only probes only: Chrome Web Store reachability (a HEAD request carrying no data) and an anonymous GitHub release check. No account information is ever uploaded.
options.about.shareCopied: Share message copied (product page and store link included)
options.about.license: © 2026 Better. Released under GNU GPL-3.0 (version 3 only, not 'or any later version').
options.domainMatch.offDesc: Only show accounts whose URL exactly matches the current domain. Accounts with an empty URL are always shown, so test environments stay strictly isolated.
options.domainMatch.wildcardDesc: Additionally show accounts whose URL is written as *.qq.com — you decide per account which ones may span subdomains.
options.domainMatch.sameMainDomainDesc: When the current domain has no accounts, show the root domain (qq.com) first, then other subdomains (music.qq.com), labelling the source in the list.
options.domainMatch.warning: fat.example.com and uat.example.com share one root domain, so test-environment accounts will appear together. Pick the wildcard tier if you need isolation.
options.domainMatch.portLooseDesc: Accounts on different ports of the same domain stay visible to each other. Loopback hosts are the exception: localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] count as one machine, and an account that declares a port appears only on that port — write localhost:* to cover every port.
options.domainMatch.portStrictDesc: An account whose URL declares a port (e.g. example.com:8443) appears only on that port. Accounts without a port appear only on the domain's default port (80 for http, 443 for https). localhost follows the same rule as every other host — write localhost:* to let one account cover every port on your machine.
options.domainMatch.portWarning: Once enabled, accounts written without a port (e.g. example.com) will not appear on non-default ports such as example.com:8443. To scope an account to one port, write its URL with the port.

options.disclaimer.title: Security Notice
options.disclaimer.desc: Account Password Helper is built for development, testing and everyday sign-in scenarios. All password data stays in your browser, encrypted field by field with AES-256-GCM, and is never uploaded to any server. For the safety of your assets, we recommend not storing highly sensitive credentials (banking, payment, etc.) in any browser extension.
options.validity.title: Session Validity Settings
options.validity.alertDesc: Set how long the session stays cached after master password verification; no re-entry needed within the validity period
options.validity.tip: This setting affects the session cache duration
options.idleLock.idleTip: After continuous inactivity beyond the set time, the session is cleared and the password manager locks automatically; the system locking or screensaver activating also locks it immediately
options.idleLock.restartTip: When enabled, the master password is required again after fully closing and reopening the browser (more secure); when disabled, you stay signed in within the validity period.
options.idleLock.diskNote: While you stay signed in, the key material that restores the session stays on this device's disk alongside the ciphertext (that is exactly what makes restarts password-free): any program that can read this browser profile can decrypt your data in the meantime. Locking or letting the session expire destroys it immediately. On a shared computer, keep this switch on.
options.identityAccess.title: Personal Info Vault Verification
options.identityAccess.policyAlways: Ask for the master password every time
options.identityAccess.tipAlways: The master password is required every time the personal info vault opens, whether or not the session is still valid. Keep this on shared or multi-user machines.
options.identityAccess.tipPerSession: The master password is required the first time the personal info vault opens after you unlock; reopening it in the same session asks nothing further. Locking, session expiry, and reloading or reopening the options page all require it again.
options.identityAccess.tipFollowValidity: Opening the personal info vault no longer asks for the master password on its own — it opens whenever the global session is still valid.
options.identityAccess.cautionFollowVali: This setting gives up the extra protection for the case where the session is unlocked but you stepped away: anyone who can operate this unlocked computer can open the personal info vault and read ID numbers, card numbers and other sensitive details. Not recommended on shared computers.

options.shortcuts.intro: For security reasons, browsers do not let extensions change their own shortcuts. To rebind a key, click "Edit Shortcuts" below to open the browser's built-in shortcut manager; reopen this dialog afterwards to see the updated status.

options.guide.productLead: Account Password Helper is a local-first password manager for your browser: accounts, passwords, TOTP codes and personal info records live only in this browser on this computer, and encryption, search, filling, health checks and backups all run locally.
options.guide.pointLocal: Your data never leaves this machine Sensitive fields are always stored on disk as AES-256-GCM ciphertext, and every encryption operation uses the browser's native Web Crypto. The extension neither stores nor uploads any account, password or verification code, and everything keeps working offline.
options.guide.pointFill: Four ways to fill Pick the side panel, the inline dropdown, the one-keystroke shortcut or the context menu. Search matches username, tags, notes and URL, and understands full pinyin as well as initials. Cross-subdomain matching comes in three tiers, and when auto-detection picks the wrong fields you can pin CSS selectors for that site.
options.guide.pointAudit: Security checkup One click scans for weak passwords, reuse, common leaked passwords (offline dictionary) and entries that haven't been rotated, then produces a 0-100 score. Every finding has a "Fix" action, and stale entries can raise an expiry reminder.
options.guide.pointBackup: Backup and migration Import and export CSV or JSON, with automatic recognition of exports from Chrome, LastPass, Bitwarden and 1Password. The encrypted .aph backup and .aphid personal info backup can be stored offline, and deleted entries stay in the trash for 30 days.
options.guide.pointWarn: The master password cannot be recovered It is only used to derive the decryption key on this machine; the extension never stores it and cannot reset it for you. If it is lost, first try the password hint you left when setting it up, then reopen an encrypted backup (.aph) using the password that was current when you exported it. Only when neither route works can you erase the data and start over — so keep exporting encrypted backups.
options.forgot.title: Forgot your master password?
options.forgot.lead: Keep the original vault while checking your recovery options. Verify that a backup opens before considering a reset. Resetting all data does not recover your password: it irreversibly deletes local data.
options.forgot.recallTitle: Go back to the unlock screen and read your hint
options.forgot.recallBody: You saved a password hint. After a few failed attempts it appears under the input field — follow it to recall the master password before wiping anything.
options.forgot.backupBody: The backup password is the master password used at export time. Later master password changes do not change it. You must remember that export-time password to open the file. If it is the same as your current master password and you have forgotten it, the backup cannot be opened either.
options.forgot.backupStep1: First select a .aph or .aphid file below and enter its export-time master password to verify decryption and structure;
options.forgot.backupStep2: After verification, we recommend importing on another device or in a separate browser profile and checking the contents, while keeping the original vault and backup file;
options.forgot.backupStep3: Only as a last step, after confirming the data you need is restored and accepting the loss of anything not backed up, consider erasing the original vault. Do not erase it just to retry a failed check.
options.forgot.backupWarn: Verification only confirms that this file decrypts and has a valid structure, not that it contains all current data. A backup is an export-time snapshot. A .aph file excludes personal information, trash and change history; verify and restore personal information separately with .aphid. Password imports append without deduplication.
options.forgot.csvTitle: Restore from a CSV / JSON export
options.forgot.csvBody: If you kept a plaintext CSV / JSON export, import and check it on another device or in a separate browser profile first, without erasing the original vault. Password exports exclude the personal info vault and only cover export time. Email attachments may be encrypted .aph files; verify those using the steps above.
options.forgot.resetTitle: No usable recovery option: consider erasing only as a last resort
options.forgot.resetBody: Even without a backup, you may choose to erase and start over, but this is not recovery. All local passwords, personal information, trash, change history and settings will be irreversibly deleted. The destructive action below still requires two confirmations.
options.forgot.checkOnly: Verification only — not imported. This does not modify or erase the original vault or display the backup's plaintext.
options.forgot.checkPassword: Master password used to export this backup
options.forgot.checkUnsupported: Only .aph password backups and .aphid personal info backups are supported.
options.forgot.checkPasswordRequired: Enter the master password used to export this backup.
options.forgot.checkFailed: Unable to verify this backup. Check the file and try again; do not erase the original vault to retry.
